Class MKCSlot

java.lang.Object
net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot
com.trevlar.menukit.core.MKCSlot
public class MKCSlot extends net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot
A vanilla Slot to the outside world. Carries its coordinates in the hierarchy as final fields and delegates behavior to its owning SlotGroup.

This is the substitutability contract in code. Every override either calls super or delegates in a way that preserves vanilla's behavioral contract:

  • mayPlace — group policy AND super (mixin chain composes)
  • mayPickup — group policy AND super
  • getMaxStackSize — min of group limit and super
  • getItem — returns EMPTY when inert, otherwise super
  • isActive — returns false when panel is hidden

A mod that mixins into Slot.mayPlace to add a global filter sees its filter run on MenuKit slots via the super.mayPlace call. The most restrictive answer wins. A mod iterating slots sees inert MenuKit slots as empty, which is a valid state for any slot.

Part of the canonical MenuKit hierarchy: Screen → Panel → SlotGroup → MKCSlot

    • setRenderPosition

      public void setRenderPosition(int x, int y)
      Moves this slot's presentation position at runtime (§0047 — position is mutable presentation; the slot's vanilla Slot.x/y identity and its sync are untouched). Client-side: the slot render + input helpers follow this immediately. Call per frame to drive a layout that depends on runtime state — e.g. a row that re-centers as its count changes. The server neither renders nor needs it.

    • isInert

      public boolean isInert()
      Returns true when this slot's panel is hidden. An inert slot is indistinguishable from a non-existent one to the outside world: getItem returns EMPTY, canInsert returns false, quick-move skips it.

      Exposed for well-behaved third parties that want to check explicitly rather than relying on the behavioral methods.

    • mayPlace

      public boolean mayPlace(net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack)
      Can this stack be placed in this slot?

      Resolves the GATING behavior from the engine by this slot's address() and AND-composes with super — so a mixin on Slot.mayPlace still runs via the super call, and the most restrictive answer wins. The gate (not this slot) holds the behavior; an un-gated slot resolves to SlotGate.OPEN = pure vanilla. This is the direct-click insertion point for a created slot (the menu seams cover shift-click/automation).

      public int getMaxStackSize(net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack)
      Max stack size for this slot, given a specific item.

      The GATING gate may cap it (absorbing the old policy stack limit); re-clamped to vanilla's own limit (including any mixin modifications via super), so a gate can lower but never raise the cap.

    • getItem

      public net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack getItem()
      Returns the item in this slot, or ItemStack.EMPTY when the panel is inert. This is the data-level inertness — hidden panels' backing storage is never exposed to the world.

      Why this override is load-bearing. Behavioral inertness (isActive() false, mayPlace(ItemStack) false, mayPickup(Player) false) blocks interaction but not observation. Without this override, any caller that reads slot.getItem() on a hidden slot — vanilla broadcastChanges syncing to the client, foreign mixins on Slot.getItem, consumer code iterating menu.slots — sees the real backing content. That leaks per-player state held in hidden-panel storage (e.g., lock metadata, private inventories, sort state) across the client-server boundary and through arbitrary mod hooks.

      Falsifying to EMPTY while inert closes that seam. When the panel becomes visible, broadcastChanges detects the change and pushes real content to the client. This is a deliberate, localized falsification — the backing Storage still holds the truth, accessible via the storage directly for consumer code that owns the panel.

      Contract: inertness is "hidden == invisible to the world" — interaction and observation. Both layers are load-bearing for the library's canonical inertness guarantee (see /mkverify all's Inertness + SyncSafety probes).

      Overrides:
      getItem in class net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot

    • isActive

      public boolean isActive()
      Returns whether this slot is active (visible and interactable).

      When false, vanilla skips this slot for rendering and hover detection. Combined with getItem() returning EMPTY while inert, this makes hidden slots truly invisible to the world.
